title: Platform differences
summary: Platform.OS and Platform.select, platform-specific files, safe areas, the Android back button and the behaviours that differ between iOS and Android.

sections.title: Detecting the platform
sections.body: `Platform.OS` is `'ios'`, `'android'` (or `'web'` and others with out-of-tree platforms). `Platform.Version` is a number on Android (the API level) and a string on iOS. `Platform.select({ ios, android, native, default })` returns the value for the current platform: a specific key wins, then `native`, then `default`.

sections.title: Platform-specific files
sections.body: When code differs a lot, split the file. The bundler resolves `import Picker from './Picker'` to `Picker.ios.tsx` on iOS, `Picker.android.tsx` on Android, then `Picker.native.tsx`, then `Picker.tsx`. Keep the same exported API in every variant.

sections.title: Real differences to plan for
sections.body:
- Shadows: iOS uses `shadow*` props; Android uses `elevation`.
- Safe areas: notches, rounded corners and home indicators need insets; use a safe area provider rather than hard-coded padding.
- Back: Android has a system back button or gesture; handle it with a `BackHandler` listener when a screen needs to intercept it.
- Keyboard: `KeyboardAvoidingView` usually needs `behavior="padding"` on iOS and often nothing on Android, where the window resizes.
- Permissions, notifications and file paths differ, so wrap them behind one module.
- Fonts and default text rendering differ slightly, so test on both.

sections.title: Practising it here
sections.body: Exercises here run as TypeScript in a browser sandbox with no React Native runtime, so they model this logic as plain functions and reducers. The same functions drop straight into a real app: call them from a component, a hook or a store. The exercise re-implements `Platform.select` and the bundler's file resolution order as pure functions.

pitfalls: Assuming `Platform.Version` is the same type on both platforms.
Hard-coding status bar or notch heights instead of reading safe area insets.
Giving platform-specific files different exports, which only fails on one platform.

gotchas.question: On Android, what does `Platform.select({ ios: 1, native: 2, default: 3 })` return?
gotchas.answer: `2`. There is no `android` key, so `native` is next, before `default`.

gotchas.question: You have `Button.native.tsx` and `Button.android.tsx`. Which does iOS use?
gotchas.answer: `Button.native.tsx`. iOS has no `.ios` file, so the resolver falls back to `.native` before the plain file.

gotchas.question: Why does a shadow show on iOS but not Android?
gotchas.answer: Android ignores the `shadow*` style props (except on recent versions with limited support for `shadowColor`). Use `elevation` there.
